title: How to make a formula return blank instead of zero
task: Keep a results column clean — show nothing (not 0) when there's no data or the inputs are empty.
keywords: formula return blank not zero excel

excel.note: Guards on the empty input. To blank ANY zero result: =IF(A2*B2=0,"",A2*B2).

explanation: The IF checks whether the source cell is empty: when A2 has data it does the calculation (5 x 4 = 20, as verified here), and when A2 is empty it returns "" instead of 0, leaving the cell looking blank. That keeps summary columns and charts tidy while a sheet is still being filled in. Two things to know: the "" result is TEXT that only LOOKS blank — ISBLANK reports it as non-empty, though SUM still ignores it. If you only want to hide zeros visually while keeping the real number underneath, use a custom number format (0;-0;;) or the display-zero-as-a-dash approach instead of changing the value.
